title: How a Motion Sensor Light Works in 60 Seconds 💡🚶 #shorts
description:
A motion sensor light doesn't see movement, it feels body heat. A Fresnel lens splits the yard into zones, and a pyroelectric sensor with two halves notices when a warm body moves from one zone to the next. A daylight sensor keeps it off during the day and a timer switches it off when you leave. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#motionsensor #securitylight #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A motion sensor light can't actually see you. It *feels* your *body heat*.

steps.label: Heat
steps.text: Every warm body gives off *infrared* energy, invisible to our eyes.

steps.label: Lens
steps.text: A bumpy *Fresnel lens* splits the yard into many invisible *zones*.

steps.label: Sensor
steps.text: Behind it, a *pyroelectric* sensor has two halves that compare heat.

steps.label: Trigger
steps.text: Walk from one zone to the next and the halves *disagree*, so the lamp *switches on*.

steps.label: Timer
steps.text: A *daylight sensor* keeps it off by day, and a *timer* turns it off after you leave.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Heat, zones, *light*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
